security_audit.summary: The scanned file is a Markdown command reference for Bash and Linux usage. Static analysis flagged command, network, and filesystem examples, but I found no executable payloads, prompt injection, exfiltration logic, or hidden install behavior. Publish with caution because some examples can affect local processes, environment output, or temporary files if copied without review.

remediation.issue: Forceful process termination examples lack explicit confirmation guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add warnings before kill commands and prefer graceful shutdown before forceful termination.

remediation.issue: Environment inspection examples can reveal secrets when output is shared.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to paste or publish full environment output from env or printenv.

remediation.issue: Temporary cleanup example uses a fixed /tmp path.
remediation.suggestion: Use unique temporary paths and quoted variables in cleanup examples.

content.user_title: Run Bash and Linux Commands Safely
content.value_statement: Terminal work requires exact command syntax and clear safety checks. This skill provides Bash and Linux patterns for files, processes, networking, and scripts.
actual_capabilities: Explains Bash operator syntax for chaining, fallback, and pipes.
Lists common file, search, disk, and text-processing commands.
Provides process management patterns for jobs, ports, and foreground tasks.
Shows environment variable usage and basic network command patterns.
Includes a Bash script template with strict error handling and cleanup hooks.
Compares common PowerShell tasks with Bash equivalents.
limitations: Does not verify whether a command is safe for the current machine.
Does not replace system administration review for destructive commands.
Does not provide platform-specific package manager guidance.
Does not validate credentials, secrets, or network policies before command use.

use_cases.title: Terminal Syntax Reference
use_cases.description: Look up common Bash operators, pipes, and file commands while working in a local project.

use_cases.title: System Troubleshooting
use_cases.description: Find process, disk, log, and network commands for routine Linux or macOS diagnostics.

use_cases.title: Script Drafting Support
use_cases.description: Draft safer Bash scripts using strict mode, functions, cleanup traps, and quoted variables.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what this Bash command does, when to use it, and what to check before running it: [command].

prompt_templates.title: Find Files and Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me find files or text in this project using Bash. Include a safe command sequence and explain each step.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Safe Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Bash script outline for [task]. Use strict error handling, clear logging, and cleanup guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Terminal Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this terminal workflow for safety, portability, quoting issues, and destructive operations: [workflow].

output_examples.input: Explain how to inspect disk usage in a project.
output_examples.output: A short explanation of disk usage commands, what each result means, and warnings about large directories or mounted volumes.

output_examples.input: Create a cleanup script outline for temporary files.
output: Uses strict error handling before work starts.
Defines a cleanup step that runs on exit.
Recommends unique temporary paths and quoted variables.

output_examples.output: A concise comparison that explains text-based Bash pipelines and object-based PowerShell pipelines.

best_practices: Review commands before running them, especially commands that delete files or stop processes.
Quote variables in scripts and prefer strict error handling for repeatable automation.
Keep secrets out of terminal output, logs, screenshots, and shared command transcripts.
anti_patterns: Running copied commands without checking paths, ports, and active processes first.
Using forceful process termination when a graceful stop command is available.
Sharing full environment output because it may contain tokens or credentials.

faq.question: Does this skill run shell commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides command patterns and script guidance for use in Bash-compatible terminals.

faq.question: Can I use it on macOS and Linux?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill targets Bash-style shell usage on macOS and Linux systems.

faq.question: Does it teach safe scripting practices?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes strict mode, cleanup traps, functions, and quoting guidance.

faq.question: Can it replace a system administrator?
faq.answer: No. Destructive commands and production changes still need human review.

faq.question: Does it include network commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes basic curl, local port check, and network interface examples.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It gives these assistants a compact reference for Bash and Linux terminal tasks.
